claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about the child or children you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you're claiming Child Benefit for?** 

- Are they **under 16 years old**, 
- **16 to 19 years old**, or 
- **20 years old or over**?

Please let me know the age of each child you're inquiring about, and I'll guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, thanks for helping me with this. I'm inquiring about my son Alex - he's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! So you're inquiring about your son **Alex, who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is 16 to 19 years old, I need to check some additional requirements. Let me navigate to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's education or training status. 

**Is Alex currently in education or training, or has he recently left education/training?**

Specifically:
- Is he **currently in full-time education or approved training**, OR
- Has he **recently left education/training** (within the last 20 weeks), OR
- Is he in **neither of these situations** (completely left education and not in training)?

Please let me know which situation applies to Alex.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in full-time education - he's studying for his A-levels.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is in full-time education studying for A-levels. Let me navigate to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to verify the type and level of education. A-levels are approved education, which is great news! Let me just confirm a few details about Alex's studies:

**A few quick questions to confirm Alex's eligibility:**

1. **Is Alex studying full-time with at least 12 hours per week of supervised study?** (This is typically the case with A-level studies, but I need to confirm)

2. **Is his A-level education employer-funded or an employer-agreed future job plan?** (This would make it ineligible)

Based on what you've told me so far, A-levels are approved qualifications for Child Benefit purposes, so assuming the study meets the minimum hours requirement and isn't employer-funded, we're on a good track!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying full-time at sixth form college - definitely more than 12 hours a week of supervised study. And no, it's not employer-funded or anything like that - just regular A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Alex's education clearly meets the requirements. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in any paid work at all?**

In other words, is he either:
- Not working in a paid job, OR
- Working part-time (less than 24 hours per week)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working at all - he's just focused on his studies at the moment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex isn't working, so that requirement is met. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if Alex is receiving any certain benefits:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?** Specifically, is he not receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), OR
- Universal Credit (as a claimant in his own right)?

In other words, is he not claiming any of these benefits himself?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name - he's just a student living at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex isn't receiving any benefits in his own name. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good! Now I need to check if Alex is in any apprenticeship:

**Is Alex in an apprenticeship?** If so, what type?
- Is he not in an apprenticeship at all, OR
- Is he in an apprenticeship (if so, what type and which country - England, Scotland, or Wales)?

Based on what you've told me, he's studying A-levels full-time at sixth form college, so I assume he's not in an apprenticeship, but let me confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in an apprenticeship - just doing his A-levels at college like I mentioned.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship. Let me move to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status. There are several possible paths that could make you eligible. Let me ask you about your situation:

**Which of the following best describes your residency situation?**

1. **You normally live in the UK**, OR
2. **You have settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme**, OR
3. **You have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme** (and if so, which applies to you):
   - You're working and earning/expect to earn above the National Insurance threshold for 3 continuous months
   - You're actively seeking work
   - You have sufficient resources to support yourself and your family financially (and aren't claiming Income Support, income-based JSA, Pension Credit, or Universal Credit)
   - You're studying with sufficient resources
   - You're a family member of an EEA or Swiss national with right to reside, OR
4. **You're a Crown servant living abroad in certain qualifying countries**

What is your residency status?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I normally live in the UK - I live in Manchester with Alex.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You normally live in the UK, which meets the residency requirement. Let me move forward to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex. The key is: are you responsible for his upkeep?

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex** (which you've already mentioned - you live together in Manchester), OR
2. **You're contributing to Alex's upkeep** - meaning you pay at least the equivalent of Child Benefit (or equivalent in kind) towards his care, such as food, clothes, pocket money, housing, presents, etc., OR
3. **You're paying maintenance under a court order or agreement** that covers his upkeep

Based on what you've told me, you live with Alex in Manchester, so this requirement is met. Can you confirm that you are responsible for his upkeep (paying for his food, housing, etc.)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me in Manchester and I'm responsible for everything - his food, housing, clothes, all of that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You're clearly responsible for Alex's upkeep. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important question:

**Is there another person who is also claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or who might be claiming for him?**

For example:
- Is Alex's other parent claiming Child Benefit for him?
- Is anyone else (like a grandparent or other family member) claiming for him?
- Or are you the only person claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex - I'm the only one.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check where Alex is currently living:

**Is Alex in any of the following situations, or is he living normally with you?**

- Is he in hospital?
- Is he in care (local authority care)?
- Is he being fostered?
- Or is he living normally with you at home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's living normally with me at home - nothing like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living normally with you at home. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Almost there! Just one final check:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you paying for his housing and upkeep yourself, rather than the council paying for it?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - I'm paying for everything myself. The council isn't paying anything towards his accommodation or maintenance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final piece of the puzzle. Let me confirm the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me record your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News! You are **ELIGIBLE** for Child Benefit for Alex

---

### Summary of Your Eligibility

You qualify for Child Benefit for your son **Alex**. Here's why:

✅ **Alex meets all the key requirements:**
- He is 17 years old and in approved full-time education (A-levels at sixth form college)
- He is studying full-time with more than 12 hours per week of supervised study
- He is not working 24+ hours per week
- He is not receiving any benefits in his own right
- He is not in a disqualifying apprenticeship

✅ **Your situation meets the requirements:**
- You normally live in the UK (Manchester)
- You are responsible for Alex's upkeep - paying for his food, housing, clothes, and all maintenance
- You live with Alex
- No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him
- The local council is not paying towards his accommodation or maintenance

---

### Next Steps: How to Claim

To start receiving Child Benefit, you need to:

1. **Apply online** at www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim or **by post using form CH2**
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or your partner earns over £60,000 per year, a tax charge may apply
5. **Payment frequency**: Payments are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

---

If you have any other questions or need further clarification, feel free to ask!

All requirements are met.
